headline: Steel pricing surge narrows losses, margins turn positive
summary_short: Cleveland-Cliffs' Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 5.9% y/y to $5,226M as domestic HRC pricing hit its highest quarterly average since 2022, swinging gross profit to $132M (+$344M y/y) and narrowing the net loss to $145M (diluted EPS -$0.25) from $486M a year ago.
summary_long: Revenue grew $292M (6%) y/y to $5,226M, driven by higher steel pricing (+$240M, avg selling price $1,124/net ton) and favorable mix as the low-margin ArcelorMittal USA semi-finished slab contract concluded, and higher scrap-business revenue, partly offset by a 6% drop in steel shipment volumes. Consolidated gross margin swung to +$132M (+$344M y/y) on the pricing gain and lower idle-facility charges, partially offset by elevated repair/maintenance costs. Operating loss narrowed to $49M and Adjusted EBITDA rose to $266M. Net loss narrowed to $145M ($0.25/share) from $486M ($0.98/share). Cash rose to $70M q/q; long-term debt held roughly flat at $7,703M. Management guided next-12-months capex to approximately $900M, primarily sustaining spend including the Burns Harbor C blast furnace reline.

drivers.explanation: Higher steel pricing (+$240M, HRC avg selling price $1,124/net ton) and favorable mix as the ArcelorMittal USA slab contract ended, plus higher scrap revenue, partly offset by a 6% drop in shipment volumes.
Higher HRC pricing lifted revenue and cost of goods sold fell on a net decrease in idle-facility charges versus the prior-year quarter, partly offset by elevated repair and maintenance costs.
Steelmaking segment Adjusted EBITDA rose primarily due to the increased gross margin from operations, which included a net decrease in idled-facilities charges.
Loss narrowed mainly on the gross-margin improvement described above; income tax benefit fell $128M y/y as the pre-tax loss shrank, partially offsetting the operating improvement.

Improving domestic steel market conditions (higher HRC pricing, subdued imports, Section 232 tariffs) drove the swing toward profitability; the company continued footprint optimization (idling Gary finishing line, consolidating Burns Harbor plate mills) to support margins.
